title: UN Security Council Attributes 2025 Red Fort Blast to Al-Qaeda Subcontinent
summary: The United Nations Security Council (UNSC) has officially attributed the November 2025 blast near Delhi's Red Fort to Al-Qaeda in the Indian Subcontinent (AQIS). This attribution comes from the 38th report of the UNSC's Analytical Support and Sanctions Monitoring Team, published on Monday. The blast on November 10, 2025, killed 11 people and injured several others. This marks the first time a UN document has linked the attack to AQIS. The report states that AQIS has evolved from a fragmented group into a regional terrorist organization, strengthening its logistical and financial networks. The group operates through decentralized, small, and dispersed cells instead of large units. The report also raised concerns over AQIS's efforts to use Bangladesh as a base for establishing cells. The National Investigation Agency (NIA) continues its probe into the attack. The NIA has alleged that those chargesheeted in the case were linked to Ansar Ghazwat-ul-Hind (AGuH), which the agency describes as an offshoot of AQIS. Umer Un Nabi. However, the charges against the accused are yet to be judicially tested, with the court yet to take cognizance of the NIA chargesheet. The UNSC report also mentioned that Al-Qaeda and ISIL (Da'esh) have maintained an interest in developing chemical and biological weapons for years, but have so far been unable to overcome technical difficulties. Instructions for producing such weapons have been widely circulated among online terrorist communities. For example, in February, ISIL (Da'esh)'s English-language Invade magazine included instructions on how to develop botulinum toxin and cyanide. ISIL-K has shown a particular interest in ricin, circulating instructions on developing the toxin over the past 12 months.

title: Trump Signs Executive Order Overhauling Childhood Vaccine Recommendations
summary: US President Donald Trump signed an executive order on Monday recommending a reduction in the number of diseases covered by universal routine childhood vaccination recommendations from 18 to 11. The order also advocates for splitting the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine into three separate shots, to be administered at separate visits. Separate measles, mumps, and rubella vaccines are currently not available in the US. Marco Cavaleri, head of the European Medicines Agency's Public Health Threats Department, stated that such decisions could lead to immunization gaps, leaving populations vulnerable to outbreaks and fueling mistrust in vaccines. The order moves recommendations for COVID-19, influenza, rotavirus, meningococcal disease, RSV, and hepatitis An and B away from universal routine vaccination. Some immunizations will remain recommended for children considered at higher risk, while others will be subject to "shared clinical decision-making" between parents and healthcare providers. The World Health Organization (WHO) chief, Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, stated on Wednesday that the current evidence is "unequivocal: vaccines, including the MMR vaccine, are safe and do not cause autism." He added that delaying vaccines or separating doses unnecessarily does not make vaccination safer and can leave children unprotected. Trump's Health Secretary, Robert F. Kennedy Jr., has questioned vaccine safety and promoted claims linking vaccines to autism. Trump claimed, without evidence, that the current combined MMR shot could be "quite lethal." The executive order is an attempt to reinstate sweeping changes to the vaccine schedule made earlier this year by Kennedy Jr., which a federal judge later halted. However, an executive order can only offer guidance to agencies and does not change laws or set recommendations. Recommendations from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the federal agency that sets vaccine guidance, remain the same. Noele Nelson, a public health professor at Cornell University, said the primary effect of the order has been "adding unnecessary confusion" and "undermining trust in vaccines." The US is experiencing a resurgence of measles, with 2,465 confirmed cases reported as of August 6, 2026, after the disease was eliminated over 25 years ago.

He rejoined Thrive Capital, Kushner's venture capital firm, earlier this year after leaving Disney. Kushner, 41, is the founder of Thrive Capital and the younger brother of Jared Kushner. title: West Bengal Government Revokes Ananta Maharaj's Award Over Netaji Remarks
summary: The West Bengal government withdrew the Banga Bibhushan award from Nagendra Ray, known as Ananta Maharaj, on August 13. title: ICE Plans $20 Million Purchase of Electric Shock Gloves for Agents
summary: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) plans to outfit its officers and agents with electric-shock gloves, with the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) seeking between $10 million and $20 million for the purchase. The devices can deliver up to 380 volts of electricity and up to 30 pulses per second, activated by a button. They also feature built-in microprocessors that record activation. A user manual for the G.L.O.V.E. recommends avoiding use on the elderly, small children, pregnant women, and the "severely handicapped," and suggests an additional officer be present to restrain the subject. The device must make direct contact with a subject's skin but can function through thin clothing layers when wet. A DHS spokesperson stated that ICE is "constantly assessing the needs of our officers in the field to ensure they have the tools and equipment necessary to safely arrest and remove criminal illegal aliens from our country." title: Netanyahu Rejects Trump's 15-Point Gaza Plan, Citing Hamas Disarmament

The plan, backed by the United States, calls for the Israeli military to gradually withdraw from parts of Gaza as Hamas disarms. Netanyahu insists the army will not withdraw from Gaza before Hamas is "genuinely disarmed" of both heavy and light weapons. He stated Israel's military "will not carry out any withdrawal until Hamas is genuinely disarmed." Donald Trump's 15-point framework is based on reciprocal steps, including Hamas surrendering its weapons within a transitional arrangement, the formation of an international stabilization mechanism and a Palestinian security structure, and progressive Israeli force withdrawal as the new order becomes operational. The proposal from President Donald Trump's Board of Peace suggests decommissioning Hamas's heavy weapons, factories, depots, and tunnels through a "gradual, sequential and time-bound" process, monitored by an International Verification Committee and supported by an international stabilization force. Each phase depends upon verified completion of the previous phase, with Israeli withdrawal linked to that process and proceeding in stages alongside it. Netanyahu's rejection comes ahead of elections in October, where he faces flagging popularity. His decision is seen as a balancing act between pleasing Donald Trump and his right-wing base. Trump insists his relationship with Netanyahu remains "very good" despite the Gaza rift. Netanyahu recently selected Oren Dobronsky for a Likud Knesset slot; Dobronsky previously called Trump a "morally corrupt piece of shit." title: Trump Confirms Secret Plane Switch in Turkey Amid Iran Missile Threat
summary: President Donald Trump confirmed Tuesday that he was instructed to switch planes after reports detailed his secret move to a decoy aircraft during his departure from a NATO summit in Turkey in July. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, Natalie Harp, Walt Nauta, and Dan Scavino traveled with Trump on the C-32A. title: Congo Ebola Outbreak on Track to Surpass Deadliest in History
summary: The World Health Organization (WHO) announced Wednesday that the ongoing Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo is projected to surpass the 2014-2016 West African outbreak, which killed over 11,000 people. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus stated the current outbreak is moving faster than any previous one, with Dr. Abdirahman Mahamud, WHO’s director for health emergency alert and response operations, expecting the peak in six to twelve months. The outbreak, considered the fastest-growing in history, has claimed over 2,000 lives out of more than 4,300 cases. Government data on Tuesday reported 4,449 cases and 2,061 deaths. The first 1,000 deaths occurred over nine weeks, while the second thousand took only three weeks. The outbreak was officially declared on May 15, but health authorities now say sequencing showed it began months earlier, in February. A study published in Nature Medicine on Monday identified a new variant of the Bundibugyo virus responsible for the outbreak, originating from an unknown animal source. This Bundibugyo strain has no approved vaccines or treatments, unlike the Zaire strain of the 2014-2016 outbreak. The disease is spreading in a remote part of eastern Congo, near the borders with South Sudan, Uganda, and Rwanda, an area facing ongoing conflict, poor infrastructure, and ill-equipped health centers. Misinformation and community mistrust of outsiders have kept some people from seeking care, and health workers have gone on strike over lack of pay. The UN humanitarian chief, Tom Fletcher, warned the outbreak is doubling in size every 20 days.

title: Human Rights Groups Sue Trump Administration Over ICC Sanctions
summary: Four human rights organizations filed a federal lawsuit on Tuesday challenging the Trump administration's sanctions against the International Criminal Court (ICC). The American Friends Service Committee, the Center for Constitutional Rights, Human Rights Watch, and the Open Society Institute filed the complaint in the US District Court for the Southern District of New York. The lawsuit challenges Executive Order 14203, signed by President Donald Trump in February 2025, which authorized sanctions on ICC officials and those assisting its investigations. title: Maharashtra FDA Suspends Four Domino's Outlets for Food Safety Violations
summary: The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) suspended the food business licenses of four Domino's Pizza outlets on Wednesday, including three in Mumbai, for alleged violations of food safety and hygiene norms. The fourth outlet is located in Satara district. The action was taken during a special drive targeting chain restaurants. In Mumbai, the Vile Parle West outlet faced action for deficiencies in displaying its FSSAI license, potable water, food storage, pest control, and hygiene facilities. The Borivali West outlet was found to have 15% non-compliance, with issues in food storage, temperature monitoring, food testing, cleanliness, and pest control. The Ghatkopar West outlet was deficient in cleanliness, sanitation scheduling, pest control, and failed to follow FIFO and FEFO practices, along with improper temperature control. The Malkapur outlet in Satara district had about 40% non-compliance, with deficiencies in basic facilities, equipment, cleanliness, and pest control. The FDA, headed by Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe, inspected 104 establishments across the state, including outlets of KFC, Pizza Hut, McDonald's, Subway, Burger King, Starbucks, and Monginis. During the drive, operations at two establishments were halted, 95 improvement notices were issued, and five food business licenses were suspended. Separately, Blinkit's Malad West warehouse license was suspended for expired and tampered products, and cockroach infestations. title: IEA Cuts Oil Demand Forecast; Trump Claims Hormuz Control Amid Iran Demands
summary: The International Energy Agency (IEA) on Wednesday sharply reduced its 2026 global oil demand forecast, now predicting a 1.6 million barrels per day slump, an increase from its July forecast of one million barrels. The IEA attributes this to shipping disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz and high prices. Global observed oil inventories fell below 7.9 billion barrels in July, marking the lowest level since April 2025. Supply remained 6.3 million barrels a day lower year-on-year in July. Brent crude prices reached nearly $90 per barrel on Tuesday night, up from around $70 before the war. The IEA report emphasizes the increased urgency of reopening the Strait as inventory buffers rapidly deplete. President Donald Trump stated on Wednesday that the U.S. has "total control" over the Strait of Hormuz, describing the naval blockade as a "wall of steel." Secretary of Energy Chris Wright claimed on Tuesday that the seven-day average for oil leaving the Strait of Hormuz is almost 9 million barrels per day. Wright added that total oil exports from Gulf states average about 15 million barrels per day when pipelines are included. He suggested private businesses undercount ship numbers due to covert movements. However, market research service Commodity Context tracked 7 million barrels per day by sea for the past week, while Kpler estimated only 5 million barrels per day by sea. Kpler data also shows vessel transits through Hormuz at a five-day average of around 13 on Tuesday, a near three-month low since May 12. This traffic represents about a 90% decrease from the pre-war daily average of 130 ships. Iran's top national security official Mohsen Rezaei said Tuesday that Hormuz will not open fully until Washington agrees to Tehran's demands. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi reiterated this position on Tuesday. President Trump on Monday stated he now intends to demand compensation from Iran for "all of the people that they have killed," following Iran's own demands for compensation in peace talks.

title: Young Scots Urge Prime Minister to Rethink Under-16 Social Media Ban
summary: More than 150 youth organizations and young people in Scotland have written to Prime Minister Andy Burnham, urging him to reconsider plans for an UK-wide ban on social media for individuals under 16. The Scottish Youth Parliament (SYP) led the group, warning that a total ban could push young people toward less regulated online spaces. The SYP stated that if the UK Government proceeds with the measure, young people must have a meaningful role in its implementation. The group supports measures to enhance online safety but argues that ministers have not provided sufficient evidence to demonstrate that an outright ban would achieve its intended goals. Research by the SYP found that 81% of young people believe the proposals would encourage under-16s to find riskier ways to access social media. Campaigners are also questioning the extent of youth involvement in the policy-making process. The letter was signed by organizations including the Children and Young People’s Commissioner Scotland, Children in Scotland, Together (Scotland), and Forces Children Scotland. The SYP hopes a Children's Rights impact assessment will be conducted before the ban is implemented to better understand its effects on young people in Scotland, following Holyrood's incorporation of the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child into Scots Law in 2024. Adebayo Shehu Tijani, a Nigerian Mass Communication student and film editor, shared his personal experience of discovering opportunities online before turning 16, which he believes helped shape him into a young advocate. title: Syrian Court Sentences Bashar al-Assad, Brother, Cousin to Death
summary: A Syrian court on Tuesday sentenced ousted President Bashar al-Assad and his younger brother Maher al-Assad to death in absentia for crimes against humanity and war crimes. The court convicted Bashar al-Assad of premeditated murder, torture, arbitrary detention, and crimes against humanity, including the killing of children. This ruling marks the first conviction against Bashar al-Assad or members of his inner circle since the Assad family's more than five-decade rule ended in December 2024. The 14-year conflict left about half a million people dead. Bashar al-Assad and Maher al-Assad fled to Russia after the government's fall in December 2024 and received political asylum. Syria's new rulers have asked Russia to hand the Assads over. Najib, a former Syrian army brigadier general, headed the Political Security Branch in Daraa in 2011, where the arrest and alleged torture of teenagers for anti-government graffiti became an early catalyst for the nationwide protests that developed into the civil war. title: Europe Prepares for Wednesday Solar Eclipse; Protective Glasses Scramble, Recalls Mount

Doctors warn that direct viewing of the sun during an eclipse can damage the retina, potentially harming central vision cells. The eclipse will be total in parts of Spain, Iceland, and Greenland. Other European countries, including the UK, Austria, Italy, Denmark, and Latvia, will experience a partial eclipse. The Met Office confirmed the UK will see 90 to 96 percent obscuration, the largest since 1999, with the next comparable event in 2081. title: Turkish Parliament Passes Law for PKK Member Reintegration

The entire community of Summerland, home to approximately 12,000 residents, was ordered evacuated, alongside an additional 8,000 individuals from other areas. The British Columbia government declared a state of emergency as 102 wildfires burn across the province. Nearly half of these fires are reported as out of control. Canada’s federal government announced it will provide urgent assistance to British Columbia to aid in the response efforts. The Royal Canadian Mounted Police are investigating a possible wildfire death near Summerland, though hazardous conditions have prevented authorities from confirming the fatality. Officials state the Bald Range wildfire triggered the largest evacuation event so far this summer in the region. The Bald Range wildfire nearly doubled in size, forcing 20,000 people to flee. The blaze has been described as being similar to “a bomb going off.” Firefighters continue to battle the 102 fires day and night across the province.
